'''Jiri Jonas''' (born April 1, 1932, in [[Prague]], [[Czech Republic]]) is a professor emeritus of [[chemistry]] in the Center for Advanced Study at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name="Unger"/><ref name="emeritus">{{cite web|title=Emeritus Faculty Photo Directory|url=http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/faculty/emeritusphoto.html|website=The Department of Chemistry at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|accessdate=May 2, 2016|archive-date=April 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422101644/http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/faculty/emeritusphoto.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Jiri Jonas is considered a pioneer in the use of magnetic resonance imaging at high pressure, developing techniques to study the dynamic structure of liquids and proteins.<ref name="Rechcigl"/><ref name="Unger"/><ref name="Fleming">{{cite journal|last1=Fleming|first1=Graham R.|last2=Wolynes|first2=Peter G.|title=Chemical Dynamics in Solution|journal=Physics Today|date=1990|volume=43|issue=5|pages=36|doi=10.1063/1.881234|url=http://www.cchem.berkeley.edu/grfgrp/Papers/1990%20Fleming%20PhysToday43.pdf|bibcode=1990PhT....43e..36F}}</ref> This approach has been used in the study of the arc repressor, a DNA-binding protein containing 53 amino acid residues.<ref name="Taniguchi">{{cite book|last1=Taniguchi|first1=Yoshihiro|last2=Stanley|first2=Harry E.|last3=Ludwig|first3=Horst|title=Biological Systems Under Extreme Conditions Structure and Function|date=2002|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|location=Berlin, Heidelberg|isbn=978-3-662-04802-3|pages=75–100|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WqDEPm_bTcIC&pg=PA75|accessdate=3 May 2016}}</ref><ref name="Pesquisa">{{cite journal|title=General de Napoleão|journal=Pesquisa|date=2009|url=http://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/2009/01/22/general-de-napoleao/|accessdate=May 2, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Peng">{{cite journal|last1=Peng|first1=X|last2=Jonas|first2=J|last3=Silva|first3=J L|title=Molten-globule conformation of Arc repressor monomers determined by high-pressure 1H NMR spectroscopy|journal=Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A|date=March 1, 1993|volume=90|issue=5|pages=1776–1780|doi=10.1073/pnas.90.5.1776|pmid=8446590|pmc=45962|bibcode=1993PNAS...90.1776P|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Jiri Jonas was awarded his B. S. Degree at the [[Charles University in Prague|University of Prague]] in 1956.  In 1960 he received his a PhD from the [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]], where he worked with [[Josef Pliva]].<ref name="ChemistryTree">{{cite web|title=Josef Pliva|url=http://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=78764|website=Chemistry Tree|accessdate=May 2, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Illinois"/> 
He won awards for scientific work from the academy in 1958, 1960 and 1964.<ref name="Texas">{{cite web|title=Evaluation of the Advanced Research and Advanced Technology Programs A Report to the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board|url=http://www.thecb.state.tx.us/reports/pdf/0586.pdf|website=Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board|accessdate=May 2, 2016|archive-date=January 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170125123739/http://www.thecb.state.tx.us/reports/pdf/0586.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 1966, Jonas joined became a professor at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. He became the second director of the [[Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology]] at the University of Illinois, and was instrumental in establishing it as an interdisciplinary center.  He followed [[Theodore L. Brown]], serving from August 1993 until September 2001, when he was succeeded by [[Pierre Wiltzius]].<ref name="Illinois"/><ref name=Brown2009>{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Theodore L.|title=Bridging divides : the origins of the Beckman Institute at Illinois|date=2009|publisher=University of Illinois|location=Urbana|isbn=978-0252034848|url=http://www.press.uillinois.edu/books/catalog/38tnd6hm9780252034848.html|accessdate=11 December 2014}}</ref>{{rp|xiv-xv}} His colleagues included [[Harry George Drickamer]], [[Herbert S. Gutowsky]], [[Rudolph A. Marcus]], and others.<ref name="Biographical">{{cite book|last1=Academies|first1=National Academy of Sciences, the National|title=Biographical memoirs|date=2005|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|location=Washington|isbn=978-0-309-545-38-9|page=151|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mbdTAgAAQBAJ&pg=PT151}}</ref> He married biochemist [[Ana Jonas|Ana Masiulis]] on June 1, 1968.{{citation needed|date=September 2016}}

==Research==
Working in the areas of chemical physics and physical chemistry,<ref name="Illinois">{{cite web|title=Jiri Jonas|url=http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/faculty/Jiri_Jonas.html|website=The Department of Chemistry at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|accessdate=May 2, 2016}}</ref> Jonas has been particularly interested in reaction kinetics and the behavior of liquids under extreme conditions such as high pressure and extreme heat. He is considered "a pioneer in the use of high-pressure nuclear magnetic resonance and Raman spectroscopy" which he has used to study liquids and their reactions under such conditions.<ref name="Unger"/> He has developed new experimental techniques involving 1 and 2 dimensional high-resolution and high-pressure nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy to study proteins and protein folding.<ref name="Peng"/><ref name=Eldik/> Techniques include [[Raman spectroscopy|Raman]]<ref name=Jonas1999>{{cite book|chapter=High-Pressure Raman Scattering Studies of Fluids|pages=1–23|last=Jonas|first=Jiri|editor-last1=Winter|editor-first1=Roland|editor-last2=Jonas|editor-first2=Jiri|title=High pressure molecular science|date=1999|publisher=Kluwer Academic Publishers|location=Dordrecht|isbn=978-0792358060|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FYztCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA1}}</ref> and [[Rayleigh scattering|Rayleigh]] laser scattering methods for spectroscopy,<ref name="Hegemann">{{cite journal|last1=Hegemann|first1=B.|last2=Jonas|first2=J.|title=Temperature study of Rayleigh and Raman line shapes in liquid carbonyl sulfide|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry|date=November 1984|volume=88|issue=24|pages=5851–5855|doi=10.1021/j150668a022}}</ref><ref name=Jonas1987>{{cite book|chapter=Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and Laser Scattering Techniques at High Pressure|pages=193–235|last=Jonas|first=Jiri|editor-last1=Eldik|editor-first1=R. van|editor-last2=Jonas|editor-first2=J.|title=High pressure chemistry and biochemistry|date=1987|publisher=D. Reidel Pub. Co.|location=Dordrecht|isbn=978-9027724571|doi=10.1007/978-94-009-3827-4_8}}</ref> Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR)<ref name="Zhang">{{cite journal|last1=Zhang|first1=Jing|last2=Peng|first2=Xiangdong|last3=Jonas|first3=Ana|last4=Jonas|first4=Jiri|title=NMR Study of the Cold, Heat, and Pressure Unfolding of Ribonuclease A|journal=Biochemistry|date=July 1995|volume=34|issue=27|pages=8631–8641|doi=10.1021/bi00027a012|pmid=7612603}}<!--|accessdate=May 2, 2016--></ref> and photo-chemically induced dynamic nuclear polarization (Photo-CIDNP).<ref name="Illinois"/>

{{blockquote|"The long-term objective of our work on biochemical systems is to contribute to the understanding of folding of proteins, folding intermediates and structure of pressure denatured states." Jiri Jonas<ref name="Illinois"/>}}

Jonas has been a co-director of the NATO Advanced Study Institute on High Pressure Chemistry, Biochemistry and Materials Science.<ref name="Texas"/> He has co-edited  ''High pressure chemistry and biochemistry'' (1987),<ref name=Eldik>{{cite book|editor-last1=Eldik|editor-first1=R. van|editor-last2=Jonas|editor-first2=J.|title=High pressure chemistry and biochemistry|date=1987|publisher=D. Reidel Pub. Co.|location=Dordrecht|isbn=978-9027724571}}</ref>  ''High Pressure Chemistry, Biochemistry and Materials Science'' (1993)<ref name=Winter1993>{{cite book|editor-last1=Winter|editor-first1=R.|editor-last2=Jonas|editor-first2=Jiri|title=High pressure chemistry, biochemistry and materials science : [proceedings of the NATO Advanced Study Institute on High Pressure Chemistry, Biochemistry and Materials Science, Aquafredda di Maratea, Italy, September 20 – October 3, 1992]|date=1993|publisher=Kluwer|location=Dordrecht|isbn=978-0792322900}}</ref> and ''High pressure molecular science'' (1999).<ref name=Winter1999>{{cite book|editor-last1=Winter|editor-first1=Roland|editor-last2=Jonas|editor-first2=Jiri|title=High pressure molecular science|date=1999|publisher=Kluwer Academic Publishers|location=Dordrecht|isbn=978-0792358060}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Jonas is a member of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS) (1982),<ref name="APSFellows">{{cite web|title=APS Fellowship|url=https://www.aps.org/units/dcp/fellowship/index.cfm?year=1982|website=APS Physics|accessdate=May 2, 2016}}</ref> the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (1985),<ref name="NAS">{{cite web|title=Jiri Jonas|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/jiri-jonas-tjquew/|website=National Academy of Sciences|access-date=May 2, 2016}}</ref> the American Association for the Advancement of Science (1987)<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web|title=LIST OF ACTIVE MEMBERS BY CLASS|url=https://www.amacad.org/multimedia/pdfs/classlist.pdf|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|date=October 29, 2015}}</ref> and the [[American Philosophical Society]] (2003).<ref name="Unger">{{cite news|last=Unger|first=Jeff|title=Jiri Jonas elected to American Philosophical Society|url=https://news.illinois.edu/blog/view/6367/207843|accessdate=May 2, 2016|work=Illinois News Bureau|agency=University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|date=May 30, 2003}}</ref> He was chair of the Division of Chemical Physics of the APS for the 1985–1986 term.<ref name="Chair">{{cite web|title=Past DCP Executive Committee Members|url=https://www.aps.org/units/dcp/governance/officers/past.cfm|website=APS Physics|accessdate=May 2, 2016}}</ref>

Jonas received a Guggenheim Fellowship in 1972.<ref name="Guggenheim">{{cite web|title=Jiri Jonas|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/jiri-jonas/|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|accessdate=May 2, 2016}}</ref>
Jonas was the second recipient of the Joel Hildebrand Award in 1983. The award is given by the [[American Chemical Society]] "for distinguished contributions to the understanding of the chemistry and physics of liquids."<ref name="Hildebrand">{{cite web|title=Joel Henry Hildebrand Award in the Theoretical and Experimental Chemistry of Liquids|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/joel-henry-hildebrand-award-in-the-theoretical-and-experimental-chemistry-of-liquids.html|website=American Chemical Society|accessdate=May 2, 2016}}</ref> In 1988 Jonas received an award from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation of the Federal Republic of Germany, recognizing him as a Senior U.S. Scientist.<ref name="Texas"/>

The Centro Nacional de Ressonância Magnética Nuclear Jiri Jonas (CNRMN, trans. National Center of Nuclear Magnetic Resonance of Macromolecules Jiri Jonas), founded at the University of Rio de Janeiro in 1997, is named in his honor.<ref name="CNRMN">{{cite web|title=National Center of Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Jiri Jonas|url=http://cnrmn.bioqmed.ufrj.br/|website=CNRMN|accessdate=May 2, 2016|archive-date=April 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160423161718/http://cnrmn.bioqmed.ufrj.br/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Romero">{{cite news|last1=Romero |first1=Thiago |title=O Centro Nacional de Ressonância Magnética Nuclear Jiri Jonas (CNRMN), localizado no campus da Universidade |url=http://www.aids.gov.br/noticia/o-centro-nacional-de-ressonancia-magnetica-nuclear-jiri-jonas-cnrmn-localizado-no-campus-da- |accessdate=May 2, 2016 |work=Brazilian National STD and AIDS Programme |date=September 3, 2007 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160514030914/http://www.aids.gov.br/noticia/o-centro-nacional-de-ressonancia-magnetica-nuclear-jiri-jonas-cnrmn-localizado-no-campus-da- |archivedate=May 14, 2016 }}</ref> It has been directed by [[Jerson Lima Silva]] since 1998.<ref name="TWAS">{{cite web|title=URRICULUM VITAE : JERSON LIMA SILVA|url=http://twas.org/sites/default/files/member/cv_jl_silva_october_2015.pdf|website=The World Academy of Sciences|accessdate=May 2, 2016|archive-date=June 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160601110530/http://twas.org/sites/default/files/member/cv_jl_silva_october_2015.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
